- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.10) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.10), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to align with mean-reversion bias.  
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days); apply a 2–5 day decay filter to smooth out overreaction.  
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent lag: model is typically 1–2% below true outcome in early periods (days 1–7), then converges; adjust early forecast by +1–2% for first 7 days.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated short-term volatility (e.g., alternating +0.23/-0.16), model tends to misalign with true mean; apply a sentiment-weighted smoothing factor (e.g., 0.7×sentiment + 0.3×history).  
- Avoid forecasting spikes in 30d horizon unless sentiment is strongly bullish (>0.30); otherwise, cap forecast at 1–2% above recent 7-day average.
